hypothesis: Filtering retrieved candidates that contradict explicit tender constraints before LLM reranking will reduce unsafe positive matches and improve hard-pass coverage.
why_now: Production bypasses its existing structured constraint machinery, while public failures include deterministic-requirement violations and a human-rejected selection.
expected_effect: Exclude known-incompatible candidates, abstain safely for explicit out-of-scope queries or exhausted compatible pools, and retain fail-open behavior for uncertain extraction.
expected_metric_gain: Estimated +3–10 percentage points public hard-pass and +3–7 points blind hard-pass, with reduced human-reject risk.
lesson_from_history: No prior cycles exist. Baseline evidence favors safety-aware candidate selection over retrieval tuning because no unresolved cases are proven retrieval misses.
candidate_hypotheses: Constraint-aware pre-rerank candidate gating with safe fallback (selected).
